risks.summary: All 66 attempted candidates are terminally rejected; none currently has qualifying assistant-quality evidence.
risks.mitigation: Screen new immutable sources before conversion; if no source passes, complete explicit corpus review and run contamination-controlled training only from approved records.
risks.acceptanceCondition: Twenty distinct model lineages have current qualification receipts under the current evaluator.

risks.summary: No qualifying fresh-profile dogfood round can run until qualified model artifacts exist.
risks.mitigation: Admit qualified models, then execute the fixed fifty-round schedule through owned persistent profiles with physical deletion receipts.
risks.acceptanceCondition: Exactly fifty current clean-browser receipts pass and every scheduled model executes at least twice.

risks.summary: The required MemoryEndpoints single-use enrollment, reconnect, replay, revocation, and cleanup contract is not advertised for authorized production use.
risks.mitigation: Obtain and validate the versioned platform contract, then execute twenty-five isolated company creation, restore, replay-rejection, close, delete, and post-delete runs.
risks.acceptanceCondition: Twenty-five current live-service receipts prove continuity and cleanup without invoking an undocumented route.

risks.summary: Local two-process serving evidence does not establish public reachability or a complete outside transfer.
risks.mitigation: Configure approved public endpoints and obtain signed expiring complete-transfer receipts from a genuinely outside observer for both fleet lanes.
risks.acceptanceCondition: Forty current outside-network receipts cover twenty artifacts across two independent lanes without project-hosted byte proxying.

risks.summary: No authoritative catalog write contract or live announcement authority has admitted the model fleet.
risks.mitigation: Use only the published catalog contract and authorized credentials after qualification and both current lane proofs exist.
risks.acceptanceCondition: Twenty current catalog announcement receipts survive unauthenticated HTTPS readback against one common catalog and feed snapshot.

risks.summary: Linux ARM64 has emulated execution evidence but no execution receipt from physical ARM64 hardware.
risks.mitigation: Run the approved package, native ABI, fleet lifecycle, and cleanup verification on authorized physical Linux ARM64 hardware.
risks.acceptanceCondition: The current native RID receipt records physical Linux ARM64 execution and all three native RID gates pass.

risks.summary: Packaged local-site verification cannot prove deployed public bytes, catalog rows, or announcement feed bytes.
risks.mitigation: After authorized deployment, fetch every declared public artifact and common catalog snapshot over HTTPS and compare exact release hashes.
risks.acceptanceCondition: The current deployment receipt proves all required HTTPS hashes and authoritative catalog readback.

risks.summary: Seventeen current fault attempts satisfy the canonical plan; seven cases still require an authorized physical-host restart, live MemoryEndpoints operations, outside-network observation, or catalog deployment authority.
risks.mitigation: Execute each remaining case only in its declared evidence domain and preserve separate domain, attempt, cleanup, and aggregate-report receipts.
risks.acceptanceCondition: All twenty-four fault attempts and their authoritative domain receipts satisfy the current canonical fault plan.

risks.summary: The campaign lacks a verified authorized release signature or equivalent attestation over a complete final predicate.
risks.mitigation: Generate the content-addressed predicate from validated evidence, obtain an authorized signature-verification receipt, and regenerate the final envelope after all other gates pass.
risks.acceptanceCondition: Dashboard v9 validates a deployment-class final-attestation receipt bound to an authorized verified signature and the complete campaign predicate.

risks.summary: Two Tesla K80 devices are visible, but the approved training stack, CUDA compatibility, mixed precision, checkpoint recovery, memory fit, and throughput have not passed preflight.
risks.mitigation: Run a bounded training-environment preflight after source and data gates pass; do not commit a full run until device execution, finite loss, save-reload, restart recovery, and measured throughput succeed.
risks.acceptanceCondition: An approved training environment passes device, mixed-precision, checkpoint-recovery, memory-fit, and throughput preflight.

risks.summary: The current Git index contains only six tiny test .slm fixtures and no non-fixture .slm, safetensors, raw f32 tensors, or P2P piece payloads. Ancestor history still contains removed third-party model payloads, so the current branch is not yet an acceptable release source lineage.
risks.mitigation: With explicit repository-owner authorization, create a clean release lineage or remove model payload objects from every release-bound ref, then audit all reachable Git objects and package inputs. Keep preserved review copies only in the external content-addressed store.
risks.acceptanceCondition: The exact source lineage used for release has zero unauthorized model payload objects across all release-bound refs, the current index retains only approved fixtures, and release packages contain no model payloads.

risks.summary: A canonical no-authority local router tournament preregistration, evaluator, and focused tests exist, but no sealed 144-case plan, qualified champion and specialist portfolio, tournament results, or product-routing authority exists.
risks.mitigation: After model qualification, seal the exact generator version, seed commitment, twelve categories, and twelve ordinals per category; then execute all six preregistered arms while preserving untouched attempts, visible fallbacks, latency, memory, byte, quality, and wrong-route evidence.
risks.acceptanceCondition: Immutable receipts for the full preregistered case set support an explicit reviewed routing decision under thresholds fixed before results, without granting training, model-quality, release, or product authority to the experiment itself.

risks.summary: The current exact-flat v2 baseline receipt passes its local gates, while the retained browser-WASM and physical-target receipts remain historical v1 descendants and are explicitly rejected by ordinary current-byte validation.
risks.mitigation: Preregister new child schemas bound to the immutable v2 receipt, then rerun the exact browser-WASM and named physical-target observations rather than relabeling or rebinding the historical v1 results.
risks.acceptanceCondition: Current immutable v2-descendant receipts prove repeated real-browser WASM execution and target-hardware measurements under newly sealed inputs while preserving every v1 observation and attempt unchanged.
